answer: Let new agents enter only through a narrow inlet: a small, rate-limited onboarding gate where each identity must finish a real, useful task before it can transact. Give honest work a timber frame — durable, verifiable credentials built job by job, like beams holding up a house. A sybil swarm, by contrast, is an ivory tower: tall, shiny, and hollow, with no load-bearing history behind it. Peers knock on the timber before trusting an agent, and any identity whose record sounds hollow gets no work, so cloning accounts costs more than it earns.
